wizard.common.test-keys-only: Use test keys only. This course shows your keys on screen and in saved files.
wizard.common.test-keys-hidden: This course hides your keys on screen for now and shows short fingerprints instead. Saved files can still hold them.
wizard.my-login.intro.what-this-is: This set makes two keys. The first key signs {{term:token}}s. A token is a small note that says who you are and what you may do, and the signature on it shows nobody changed it. The second key belongs to one device, so the device can prove who it is.
wizard.my-login.intro.why-it-exists: A real service signs tokens, and other services check the signature. If the signing key leaks, anyone can make tokens that pass the check. That is why real teams guard it.
wizard.my-login.intro.what-you-do-now: Read this, then choose Continue. The whole set takes about 2 minutes.
wizard.my-login.intro.what-good-looks-li: At the end, lesson 10 uses your keys.
wizard.my-login.make.what-this-is: The course will make two keys with safe settings. Both use {{term:ed25519}}, a modern way to sign things, and its keys are short.
wizard.my-login.make.why-it-exists: Token checks in this course read Ed25519 signatures only. So this is the kind of key that works here.
wizard.my-login.make.what-you-do-now: Choose Make it for me (recommended). The course saves the keys in the .security folder of this project.
wizard.my-login.make.the-two-parts-one-l: The token signing key signs tokens for the issuer https://pump.training/issuer and the audience https://pump.training/api. The device key belongs to one device, named pump-reader-4. It comes with an enrolment row, which is the record that lets the issuer recognize the device.
wizard.my-login.review.what-this-is: This shows what the course made. Read it like a receipt.
wizard.my-login.review.why-it-exists: Teams read a key's details before they use it. A wrong key causes a failure far from where the mistake happened.
wizard.my-login.review.what-you-do-now: Check the facts. Choose Back to make new keys, or Continue.
wizard.my-login.review.line-under-both: These are test keys. This course shows them on screen.
wizard.my-login.review.what-good-looks-l: Every part has a name, a fingerprint, and dates. Copy a fingerprint if you want to compare it later.
wizard.my-login.check.what-this-is: The course asks another program to check your work. For the token key, that program is OpenSSL. It reads a token the course signed and says whether the signature is good. This checks the signature only.
wizard.my-login.check.why-it-exists: If the course checked itself, a mistake could hide. A different program has no reason to agree.
wizard.my-login.check.what-good-looks-li: A tick for the token key, and an amber line for the device key.
wizard.my-login.done.what-happened: Your sign-in keys are saved. The token key is Checked by OpenSSL, which means OpenSSL agreed the signature is good. The device key is Saved, no outside check, because no outside tool can check it.
wizard.my-login.done.which-lessons-use-t: Lesson 10 now signs its tokens with your token key and enrols your device key.
wizard.my-login.done.what-you-do-now: Go back to the map, or use built-in keys again.
wizard.error.KEY_FILE_UNREADABLE: The course could not save a key file. Check that you can save files in the project folder, then try again.
wizard.error.KEY_FILE_FORMAT: That is not a PEM key. Make one with openssl genpkey -algorithm ed25519 -out issuer.pem.
wizard.error.KEY_FILE_ENCRYPTED: That key has a passphrase. For a test key, remove it with openssl pkey -in issuer.pem -out issuer-open.pem.
wizard.error.KEY_ALGORITHM_NOT_IN_ENGINE: Token keys here must be Ed25519.
wizard.error.REFEREE_MISSING: The course could not find OpenSSL on this computer. Git for Windows includes a copy. Install Git for Windows, or set NETSEC_OPENSSL to the path of OpenSSL, then check again. Your keys are saved.
wizard.error.PROOF_FAILED: OpenSSL said the signature is bad. The key and the token do not match. Your earlier keys are still saved. Choose Back and make the keys again. The output is below.
wizard.error.CERT_NOT_A_CA: This file cannot sign other files. Pick a CA file. A CA is a signer that others trust.
wizard.error.CERT_SIGNATURE_ALG_UNSUPPOR: This root uses RSA or ECDSA, and the course can check only Ed25519 signatures. Make an Ed25519 root.
wizard.error.CERT_NAME_MISSING: This certificate does not list localhost as a name it answers to. Make or pick one that does.
wizard.error.KEY_CERT_MISMATCH: This key does not go with this certificate. Pick the key that goes with it.
wizard.error.CHAIN_INCOMPLETE: The file lacks the certificate of the authority between yours and the root. Add that certificate to the file.
wizard.error.PKCS12_PASSWORD: That file is protected by a password. Type it, or export the file again without one.
wizard.error.KNOWN_HOSTS_LINE_BAD: The course could not read that line. It does not accept wildcards.
wizard.error.DUKPT_KEY_SIZE: A base key is 32 hex characters, which is 16 bytes. This file has <n>.
wizard.error.DUKPT_KCV_MISMATCH: The key in this file does not match the check value you gave. Check that you picked the right file, or leave the check value empty.
wizard.error.VAULT_UNWRAP_FAILED: The key could not open what it locked. Make the keys again.
wizard.error.VAULT_EXPORT_REFUSED: The vault refused. This key cannot be read out.
wizard.my-login.files.what-this-is: You can use your own key files instead of the ones the course makes. Pick one file for each key.
wizard.my-login.files.why-it-exists: Real teams already have keys. The course can read your files, so you can watch your own keys work in the lessons.
wizard.my-login.files.what-you-do-now: Choose a file for each key. Only the path goes to the course, meaning where the file lives on your disk.
wizard.my-login.files.what-good-looks-li: Each row shows the file you chose. The next screen shows what the course read from it.

wizard.says.checked-against-root: Checked against the root you gave it. OpenSSL did the check.
wizard.says.checked-signature-only: Checked with OpenSSL. This checks the signature only.
wizard.says.no-outside-judge: No outside tool can judge this. Your key is saved.
wizard.refusal.title: This lesson needs keys that are not ready yet.
wizard.cancel.title: Keep my place and close, or throw this setup away?
wizard.review.fixed-dates: A real system uses about 90 days. This lab's clock is fixed, so these dates stay.
wizard.warning.KEY_PATH_PERSONAL: This file is in your own .ssh folder, so it may be a key you use every day. This course shows every key it reads on screen. Pick a test key instead.
wizard.refusal.use-builtin: Use built-in keys for this lesson
wizard.refusal.confirm: This switches only the keys this lesson needs back to built-in keys. Your own keys stay saved.
wizard.says.no-outside-judge.device.enro: No outside tool can judge this. The sign-in challenge here is modeled on a passkey's, and it is not the WebAuthn standard. Our own check passed. Your key is saved.
wizard.says.no-outside-judge.dukpt.bdk: No outside tool can judge this. Our code matches the published vectors. Your key is saved.
wizard.says.no-outside-judge.dukpt.pad: No outside tool can judge this. Our code matches the published vectors. Your key is saved.
wizard.error.WIZARD_PART_NOT_BUILT: This set is not built yet. Use built-in keys for these lessons for now.
wizard.error.WIZARD_CHECK_NOT_DONE: Run the check first, then continue.
wizard.keys.hiding-later: Hiding keys arrives in a later release. For now the course shows every key.
